subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - post-call recap

Thanks again for taking the call today, Alice — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned heading into the POC: 

Summary of goals / success criteria:
- Latency: 95th percentile < 200ms for 512-token responses for customer-facing inference paths
- Cost: target blended cost <= $0.002/token for the evaluation workload
- Quality: no regression vs your current model baseline on the provided eval set (we'll run paired evals)
- Security/compliance: traffic must remain within agreed network boundaries for PII-sensitive payloads

Evaluation plan / timeline (suggested):
- Week 0: finalize environment (hosted trial vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC trial) and sign short SOW
- Weeks 1-2: provision environment + onboarding + run smoke tests
- Weeks 3-4: performance & cost benchmarking, quality evals, handoff recommendations

Environment options we discussed: 
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted trial on our public service; minimal setup, fastest time-to-value.
2) Dedicated sandbox: reserved capacity in our environment (isolated GPUs) — predictable throughput. ~3 business days to provision.
3) VPC trial: private networking (VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink), customer-managed routing, KMS integration for keys. Higher setup lead time (~5-7 business days) but meets your data-residency requirements.

I attached the Redwood POC proposal (redwood-poc-proposal.docx) with detailed scope and SOW stub. Can you confirm: 1) preferred environment, 2) target kick-off week, and 3) who from your infra/security team should own network onboarding? Once you confirm we'll queue provisioning and send the checklist to your infra lead.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0123

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-02T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - post-call recap

Hi Marissa — thanks for the summary and proposal. We reviewed internally; key points from our side:
- Data residency: we need the inference traffic for PII-bearing requests to stay inside our VPC. That pushes us toward the VPC trial option.
- Security questionnaire: our InfoSec will want the standard questionnaire answered and a short network diagram + list of IP ranges to whitelist.
- Timeline: we can target a kick-off the week of 3/15 but will need to loop in our infra lead (Tom Lee) and procurement to sign the SOW.

Please send the VPC onboarding checklist and any IP ranges/ports we need to open. Also, we have a brief procurement review process — I've CC'd procurement@acmeai.com and Tom.

Appreciate it,
Alice
Head of Platform
Acme AI
alice.zhang@acmeai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeai.com>, Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-03-03T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - post-call recap

Tom — great to meet you by email. Per Alice's ask, attaching the network requirements and a short onboarding checklist (network-requirements.pdf). Quick notes to help InfoSec: 

- High level: we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and customer-managed NAT/GW. For the trial we typically recommend VPC peering if you can accept route propagation; PrivateLink is available if you require tighter controls.
- IP ranges: we'll provide a small set of egress IPs you can whitelist for callbacks and telemetry (see attachment).
- Ports: outbound 443 to our control plane and HTTPS endpoints (we do not require inbound to your network).
- KMS: we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key management (optional for trial; recommended for production).

Proposed concrete next steps:
1) Acme confirms sign-off on the SOW + sends PO / digital signature (we included an SOW stub in redwood-poc-proposal.docx).
2) Acme infra completes the VPC checklist in network-requirements.pdf and returns network contact for on-call coordination.
3) Redwood schedules provisioning and provides temporary test creds.

If that all sounds good I'll have Rafael and Dev prepare the technical onboarding runbook and draft a kickoff agenda for 3/15.

Best,
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-03-04T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - onboarding notes

Tom/Alice/Marissa — quick technical note on provisioning timelines and what to expect from each environment option: 

Hosted trial:
- Turnaround: same-day to 1 business day.
- Pros: minimal network work, fastest path to validate API and quality.
- Cons: not suitable if traffic must stay in customer VPC.

Dedicated sandbox:
- Turnaround: ~3 business days to provision reserved capacity.
- Pros: isolated compute for predictable performance; easier to mirror production throughput.
- Cons: still runs in our network, requires contractual commitment for reserved nodes.

VPC trial:
- Turnaround: typically 5-7 business days depending on firewall and procurement response times.
- Steps: sign SOW -> exchange network questionnaire -> schedule peering/PrivateLink build -> verify routes/whitelists -> smoke tests.
- We will need:
  * VPC ID and preferred connectivity method (peering vs PrivateLink)
  * Security contact + on-call window for cutover (we recommend a 2-hour window)
  * Whitelist of the egress IPs we provide

I attached a short checklist we use for VPC onboarding (vpc-onboarding-checklist.xlsx). On Redwood's side we can prep the service account and KMS integration in parallel to reduce total time.

Rafael Mendes
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeai.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeai.com>
Date: 2027-03-05T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - sample payloads and config

Tom/Alice — a few technical clarifications to ensure the POC demonstrates realistic performance/costs: 
- Please share a sample of your typical prompt+context payloads (anonymized) and expected concurrency for the trial (e.g., 10 rps with bursts to 50).
- Tokenization: if you can provide an example of the 95th-percentile prompt length that helps us choose batching/kv-cache settings.
- Model variants: we plan to run two variants during the POC (baseline model you use today + a Redwood-verified variant tuned for latency-cost tradeoffs).
- Suggested initial config for VPC trial: 4 inference workers (NVIDIA A10x or equivalent), batching window 40ms, prefix KV cache enabled. We can adjust after baseline runs.

If you send the sample payloads I'll draft the exact benchmark commands and expected metrics to share ahead of the kickoff.

- Dev
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@acmeai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@acmeai.com>

Subject: Re: POC trial environment: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC - confirmation and kickoff

Marissa/Rafael/Dev — confirming that Acme AI will proceed with a VPC trial. Next steps from our side: 
- Procurement will review and e-sign the SOW (Procurement CC'd).
- Tom (infra) will complete the network checklist and provide VPC ID + preferred connectivity (peering vs PrivateLink) by 3/12.
- Kickoff: please schedule a 60 min kickoff the week of 3/15; Tom and I are available 3/15 morning PT.

Thanks for the clear checklist — I'll attach the signed SOW once procurement completes review. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Alice
Head of Platform, Acme AI
